findings.F1: American IPA puts main stress on look (ˈlʊk ˌʌp) instead of the particle, contradicting the note and house practice.
findings.F2: Sense 4 example hand-marks a regular, unseparated form (**looked up**), which should be unmarked.
findings.F3: Semantic adaptation note is a generic translate-each-sense list naming no specific trap.
findings.F4: look-for-phrv is listed as a synonym of the find-information sense; look for is a confusable, not a synonym (and belongs under look-v).
findings.F5: Pronoun placement (look it up, not look up it) is stated in both adaptation.grammar and learner_errors[0].
findings.F6: learner_errors[1] labels the correct sentence 'I looked for the word in the dictionary' as incorrect.
